Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The file uses HTML entities (`&quot;` and `&apos;`) to inject disguised background commands into the PKGBUILD's global scope. When `makepkg` sources this file, the `&` character in these entities is interpreted by bash as the job control background operator, instead of forming valid shell quoting. As a result, lines that appear to be simple variable assignments instead attempt to execute commands like `quot;...` and `apos;...` in the background during the sourcing step of `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. This is a supply-chain attack vector that executes arbitrary, obfuscated code at parse time.
</details>
<evidence>
pkgdesc="GNOME Shell extension showing remaining Claude plan usage in the top bar and on a desktop card"
arch=('any')
url="https://github.com/SelfRef/vibecheck"
license=('MIT')
depends=('gnome-shell')
optdepends=('claude-code: usage data source and sign-in')
makedepends=('nodejs' 'pnpm')
source=("$pkgname-$pkgver.tar.gz::$url/archive/refs/tags/v$pkgver.tar.gz")
sha256sums=('46fbd16e71cbc8bed1aa56fcea42eaeb64bf4cab2204f03e3e2b3760b6b7a93c')
</evidence>
<summary>Global scope backgrounds commands via obfuscated HTML entities</summary>
</security_assessment>

Second look for PKGBUILD (incontext):
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>The first verdict incorrectly classified the PKGBUILD as UNSAFE based on the presence of HTML entities (`"`, `'`). While these entities would cause bash to attempt background execution of commands named `quot` and `apos`, those commands do not exist in a standard environment. The background attempt would result in "command not found" errors, not in the execution of any payload that exfiltrates data, downloads remote code, or performs any of the other genuinely malicious behaviors listed in the criteria. No command substitutions, backtick expansions, `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or other dangerous constructs appear in the global scope. The PKGBUILD is syntactically malformed, but this is an error or artifact, not a supply-chain attack. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe.</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>HTML entities cause errors, not exploitation</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- HTML entities cause errors, not exploitation
